title: Your Brain Fills in Your Blind Spot, and You Never Notice
hook: Your brain constantly invents parts of the world you see.

narration.text: Your brain constantly invents parts of the world you see.
Each of your eyes has a blind spot.
It is where the optic nerve connects to the retina.
There are no light-sensing cells in that specific area.
But you do not see a blank hole in your vision.
Your brain automatically fills in the missing information.
It uses surrounding details to guess what should be there.
This is called perceptual completion, and it happens instantly.
It keeps your visual world consistent and complete.
Can you think of other ways your brain takes shortcuts?

description: Discover the surprising reason you never notice your own blind spot. Your brain is constantly working behind the scenes, inventing parts of your visual world through a process called perceptual completion, ensuring a seamless experience.
topic: Why your brain fills in your blind spot without you noticing, explaining perceptual completion.
